issues.title: Written and calculation answers flattened into one run-on box
issues.detail: Card 1 pours a five-line calculation into a single paragraph with slashes ('Cost of sales / Average stock = 8 times. Average stock × 8 = 536,000. Average stock = 536,000 / 8 = 67,000. Average stock = (? + 75,000) / 2 = 67,000. Opening stock = €59,000'). Card 2 runs the list of books together with no separators ('Sales Sales Returns General Journal Cash Book – Receipts and Payments (ii) They act as a check...'). Card 10 strings bullet points together with '•' inline. Card 4 joins two reasons with a slash and no full stop ('Failure to complete the double entry/ Errors in the ledgers Incorrect totalling...'). issues.title: Attached page shows other questions and parts

issues.detail: A grey note reads 'The examiner marks the first correct answers higher than the rest (6(3) + 2) — so what these are worth depends on how many you got.' issues.title: Official scheme image sits in the question column, away from the scheme
issues.detail: On cards 7, 9 and 10 a crop of the official scheme (drawn structures, the Kc fraction, the ICE table) appears after reveal directly under the question, above 'Open original paper' and above the empty answer box; the tick list under 'THE SCHEME' is a screen further down on the phone. It is not labelled as the answer, so it looks like part of the question. On the phone these crops are very small (card 7's three structures fit in 334px; card 10's table text is about 5px). The accompanying tick text then talks about the image instead of answering: card 9's only tick point repeats the question ('Write the equilibrium constant (Kc) expression for this reaction.') with the note 'The scheme answers this with the expression set as a fraction, which its text cannot carry; its own print is shown with the answer.'
issues.suggested_fix: Move the scheme crop inside the scheme panel under a heading 'Official marking scheme', full width, one structure per row on phones; make the tick label the answer itself ('Kc = [NH3]² / [N2][H2]³') and delete the notes about what the text cannot carry.

good.why: Typed question with correct subscripts, crisp apparatus diagram, one clear 6-mark answer.
Stem and question typed with proper ion notation; three readable procedure points (only the bracket sum lets it down).

more_issues: Stem with flattened table and equation run into a wall of text
Long explanatory notes inside tick points

issues.title: Paper footer and underscore rule pasted into the question
issues.detail: Card 1's question reads '...Give reasons for your answer. _____________________ Do not hand this up. This document will not be returned to the State Examinations Commission.' The underscores render as a long line and the footer is shown in the large question font and underlined in orange as if it were the instruction.
issues.suggested_fix: Strip the rule and the Paper X footer from the question text; scan the deck for the same 'Do not hand this up' string.

issues.title: Source text truncated and answer labels left in
issues.detail: Card 5's stem runs the heading and passage together ('Text A: The Odyssey Tell me, Muse...') and stops mid-sentence at 'the oxen of Hyperion the sun God'. Text B (the Aeneid) is not printed at all, though the question asks for an example from each text. The question ends with the stray answer-box labels 'Text A: Text B:'.
issues.suggested_fix: Show both texts in full as two labelled quote blocks (or rely on the attached passage and keep the stem to one line), and drop the 'Text A: Text B:' labels.

issues.title: Paper X opens on another question's photograph
issues.detail: The attachment is the uncropped Paper X page. Card 8 (Photograph B, Korkyra relief) opens on the cover and Photograph A, the Parthenon; Photograph B is not visible. Card 3 (OL Q3, Image D) opens on Question 2's Image C, a temple reconstruction, with only the 'Question 3 / D' heading visible. Card 2 shows the right image C but Question 3's heading and image D start below it.
issues.suggested_fix: Crop Paper X to the one photograph the question names and show it inline under the stem; keep the full booklet behind the link.

issues.title: Question depends on a part that is not shown
issues.detail: 'What is your opinion of the behaviour of Pompey in that battle?' and 'how did Pompey perform as a general in this battle?' never name the battle; the earlier part that names it is not shown and there is no stem. Card 1 refers to 'Wheeler' calling the painting a masterpiece without the quotation.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a one-line grey context stem from the question's opening (e.g. the battle named in part (a), Wheeler's remark).

good.why: Clear standalone question and six well-written marking points that directly answer it.
Label-identification question with a one-row-per-label answer key and the correct plan attached.

more_issues: No inline image for image-based questions
Scheme rows carry no marks; some are not points
Terse lower-case fragments and inconsistent controls

issues.title: Expected program output flattened into the sentence
issues.detail: Card 3's question ends '...the output may now look as follows: ******************** Times Table program ******************** Multiplications of 7 0 7 14 21 28 35 42 49 56 63', one run-on line where the paper shows a multi-line console output. Card 7 ends 'Score Password ----- -------- 1 sun 6 Sun 11 Sunshine 0 12345 11 Moonlight', a two-column table collapsed to a string with stray dash runs. Both are in the large serif question type, so the mess is prominent.
issues.suggested_fix: Render sample output in a monospace block with its original line breaks (or crop it from the paper like the code listing).

issues.title: Band-descriptor rubric printed as a run-on string
issues.detail: Level-of-response schemes show the rubric as one unpunctuated grey paragraph under the bold answer: card 3 '(ii) 10 marks (B-10 scale) 10 marks Correct response Correct insertion of row of asterisks in both locations 8 marks Almost correct response Correct implementation using solution above or similar but with minor syntax or semantic error 5 marks Response with some merit Any other reasonable attempt.'; card 7 the same pattern for a B-5 scale; cards 1, 2, 5, 6, 10 'Very good description - clear understanding demonstrated 3 marks Fair description - limited understanding 2 marks'. The mark buttons (0 5 8 10) sit below with no labels, so the student has to parse the paragraph to learn what 8 means. 'B-10 scale' is examiner jargon.
issues.suggested_fix: Lay the bands out as rows ('10 — correct: asterisks in both places', '8 — almost correct: minor syntax error', '5 — some merit') and make each row the tappable score, replacing the bare number buttons.

issues.title: Scheme crops sit in the question column and can show other parts' answers
issues.detail: After reveal, the official answer crop appears under the question, above 'Open original paper' and the empty answer box, with no 'answer' heading: card 2 (the (i)/(ii) worked answers), card 3 (model program), card 7 (two solution lines), card 9 (completed test plan), card 10 (hex conversion). On the phone the tick list is a screen further down. Card 3's model program is the solution to the whole of Q16(a): it carries tags #(i) to #(vi), so it gives away the input, if/else and range(13) answers to sibling parts and its range and print lines no longer match the program in the question. Card 7's crop (lines 75-76) is pale grey on grey and about 5px high on the phone.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the crop into the scheme panel under 'Official solution'. For multi-part solutions crop or highlight only the lines for this part (card 3: lines 3-5), or type the answer lines as a code block.

issues.title: Code listings too small on a phone
issues.detail: Card 7's 44-line program is fitted to the 330px column, giving roughly 5px line height and unreadable identifiers; card 4's 11-line listing is about 9px per line with pale red numbers; card 3's is borderline. Card 8's true/false statements and card 9's two tables are also noticeably smaller than body text on the phone. All are fine on desktop, and Enlarge exists, but the question cannot be read in place.
issues.suggested_fix: Render code as real monospace text in a horizontally scrollable block, or show only the lines the part refers to (card 7 needs lines 40-44) with the full listing behind Enlarge.

good.why: Typed stem, clean crop of the true/false grid, four full-sentence answers each ending in True/False with 1 mark.
Clear wireframe question and four short 1-mark criteria; nothing extraneous.

more_issues: Questions missing a piece or with muddled structure
Alternatives joined by slashes and dots; table answers flattened

issues.title: Part cards show the whole question, never the asked part as text
issues.detail: The question area is only an image of the full printed question with every part (a), (b), (c). No typed question text appears anywhere. On cards that ask one part (2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 11) nothing marks which part is being asked except the small 'Q9(C)' label in the header, and the sibling parts are fully visible. E.g. card 5 is Q9(c) (16 marks, a concrete test) but the crop leads with (a) strip foundation and (b) mixing/placing/compacting/curing.
issues.suggested_fix: Print the stem and the asked part as real text at app body size, and keep the picture only for the drawing/sketch the part depends on (cropped to the drawing). If the whole-question crop is kept, highlight or crop to the asked part.

issues.title: Attached page opens on the exam cover page
issues.detail: On all 12 cards the 'Read original question N' reader opens at 'PDF page 1 / 2', which is the SEC cover sheet (harp logo, 'Construction Studies Theory - Higher Level (300 marks)'). The actual question is on the second page, one tap away. The attachment's title promises the question and the first screen delivers nothing useful.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the cover page from the attached pages (attach only the question's page), or open the reader on the question page. Since the question crop is already on the card, consider removing this duplicate attachment entirely.

issues.title: Question crop is too small to read on a phone
issues.detail: The printed question is scaled to the 330px card width, so its text renders at roughly 6-7px against the app's 14-15px body text. Multi-part questions with a plan beside them (cards 6, 7, 8, 10, 12) and the dense quotation in card 9 are effectively unreadable without tapping Enlarge. On desktop the same crops are comfortably legible.
issues.suggested_fix: Typed question text plus a separate, larger crop of only the drawing; let the drawing fill the card width.

issues.title: Scheme sketch sits in the question column and is tiny on a phone
issues.detail: After reveal, the official scheme page (model sketch plus bullet answers) appears directly under the question crop, above 'Your answer', far from 'The scheme' panel it belongs to. On the phone its bullet text is about 5-6px (cards 5, 6, 10, 12 especially); in card 6 the page is long, repeats the house plan, and covers only part (b) of a complete-question card.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the scheme image inside the scheme panel under a 'Model answer from the scheme' label, crop it to the sketch (the bullet text is already retyped in the steppers), and show it full width.

good.why: Complete question where showing all parts is correct; scheme is split a/b/c with totals that add to 50 and the official PPE signs shown.
No drawing, clean two-block scheme (discussion 30 + guidelines 30) with a consistent point/discussion split.

more_issues: Examiner shorthand in scheme labels and descriptions
Dead white space on phone before 'Your answer'
Stray sliver and wall of text in the acoustics card

issues.title: Sample answers pasted in as giant tick boxes
issues.detail: Card 5 (5 marks) shows seven tick boxes of first-person sample-answer prose, the first 28 lines long on a phone; card 2 (30 marks) is one tick box containing a whole sample essay. The instruction 'Tick each part you completed' does not fit example answers, there are no marks per box, and nothing says they are alternatives rather than a required list except a grey note.
issues.suggested_fix: Present as a collapsed 'Sample answer from the scheme' block (not tick boxes), with a short list of the ideas it contains for self-checking; show how the 5 or 30 marks are awarded.

issues.title: 'No answer' essay card
issues.detail: Card 3 shows 'The scheme prints no answer for this part.' under 'Select the points you actually got', a grey paragraph, then 41 number buttons (0-40). No criteria are offered to mark against.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the general essay criteria, change the heading, and use a slider or bands instead of 41 buttons.

issues.title: Grey commentary about the scheme inside the first box
issues.detail: Each scheme starts with small grey text such as 'The examination requires every answer in CROATIAN. The paper prints the rule on page 2: "..." The scheme heads its answer "Na primjer:": what it gives is an example, not a required list.' It sits inside the first tick box above the real content and reads like an internal note.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove it; replace with a plain label 'Example answer' where needed and state the language rule once per subject.

issues.title: Paragraph references look like marks; scheme rows unlabelled
issues.detail: Card 4 lists 'a) kompleksnih (2)  b) pohranjen (3)  c) dvolične (10) ...' on a 5-mark question; the bracketed numbers are paragraph numbers in the text but read as marks. The five scheme rows are not labelled a) to e) and carry no '1m' badges.
issues.suggested_fix: Write '(odlomak 2)' / '(par. 2)', prefix each scheme row with its letter and term, show 1 mark each.

good.why: One-line question, one-line answer, right text attached.
Parts a) to e) listed one per line and five short scheme rows (needs letters and the grey note removed).

more_issues: Term or author run onto the instruction

issues.title: 'No answer' essay card
issues.detail: Card 4 shows 'The scheme prints no answer for this part.' under 'Select the points you actually got', a grey paragraph explaining that the scheme has 'no criteria, no descriptive line and no split of the part's marks', and 41 number buttons. The note also quotes the title with a different word (digitalizovaném) from the one on the card (digitálním).
issues.suggested_fix: Show generic essay criteria and a simple banded self-grade; fix the heading; reconcile the title wording with the paper.

issues.title: Grey English note repeated above every answer
issues.detail: In the five-part vocabulary cards each row begins with 'The scheme prints this as the meaning of "„prapředek“". The examination prints this question in Czech and it is answered in CZECH.' (with doubled quotation marks), then the actual one-line answer. Five repeats per card; on a phone the note takes four lines and the answer one. Other cards carry 'The examination requires every answer in CZECH. The paper prints the rule on page 2: ...' inside the tick box.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace the note with a bold label: '(a) „vůbec první“' then the answer. Drop the language sentence.

issues.title: Five sub-parts flattened into one line
issues.detail: Cards 1 and 5 read 'Vysvětlete vlastními slovy: (a) „vůbec první“ (b) „prapředek“ (c) „zkrocení ohně“ (d) „setrvávat“ (e) „prozaické vysvětlení“' as a single wrapped sentence; on the phone letters end up at line ends away from their terms. Other languages' cards list a) to e) one per line.
issues.suggested_fix: One part per line, as a lettered list, with 1 mark each shown.

issues.title: Sample answer shown as one tick box with no marks
issues.detail: Cards 2 and 3 give the scheme's sample answer as one paragraph in a single tick box under 'Tick each part you completed'; a 5-mark answer has no breakdown. Card 2's paragraph is 18 lines on a phone.
issues.suggested_fix: Label it 'Sample answer' and list the 2-3 key ideas as tickable points.

good.why: Clear single question, right text attached, compact three-sentence answer.
On desktop the five answers line up one per row; only the grey notes need to go.

more_issues: Wording mismatch between question and scheme note

issues.title: Grey language-rule note under answers
issues.detail: 'The examination requires every answer in DANISH. The paper prints the rule on page 2: "Alle svar skal skrives på dansk."' is appended to the first scheme row of every card; on card 4 it is glued to the label as 'For “englebamse”: The examination requires...'. On card 3 it expands to five lines including 'The scheme prints this paragraph under “Opgave III” and names neither title.'
issues.suggested_fix: Remove from cards; state once at subject level.

issues.title: Five-part question repeats the full sentence five times
issues.detail: Card 4 prints 'Forklar betydningen af ordet ”…” som det bruges i teksten' five times with no (a)-(e) letters, no full stops, and stray spaces after the opening quote (” genbrug”, ” fortørnede”, ” vendepunkt”); on the phone the quote mark is orphaned at a line end.
issues.suggested_fix: One instruction line, then a lettered list of the five words; trim the spaces.

issues.title: Sample answer in a single all-or-nothing box
issues.detail: Cards 1 and 2 show the expected answer as one paragraph (22 lines on the phone for card 2) with a single 5m badge, so there is no way to claim part of it.
issues.suggested_fix: Split into the 2-3 ideas (how politicians communicate / positive / negative) as separate rows.

issues.title: Footer strip shows a meaningless fragment
issues.detail: Card 1's grey strip reads 'Not claimed yet · 5 marks · ikke en sikker gevinst.' (the last four words of the answer). Card 4's strip is three truncated copies of 'Enhver rimelig forklaring (e.g. ...' plus 'and 2 more'.
issues.suggested_fix: Show just the marks outstanding, or the first words of the point, never the tail.

good.why: Essay scheme with the four criteria, their weightings and a per-criterion score picker: the model for essay cards in the other languages.
Each vocabulary answer is labelled with its word and carries 1 mark.

more_issues: Essay guidance covers only one of the two titles

issues.title: Asked part is never typed; whole question shown as one image
issues.detail: The question area is a single crop of the full printed question, section banner included ('Geologic Geometry', 'Structural Forms'). The stem and part text that exist for these cards are not printed as text. Nothing marks which part is being asked apart from the small header label (e.g. 'SECTION B Q2(D)'), so the student must find line (d) at the bottom of the picture. On card 8 the label is Q1(a) but the picture gives equal space to part (b) with its three sub-parts.
issues.suggested_fix: Print the stem and the asked part as real text at body size above the picture, and crop the picture to the photo/drawing (Fig.) only. If the full crop stays, highlight the asked part.

issues.title: Question text inside the crop is unreadable on a phone
issues.detail: Scaled to a 330px card, the printed instructions are roughly 5-6px tall against 14-15px app text. The assembly sheet (cards 5, 11) with eight dimensioned parts and a parts list is illegible at phone width; dimensions on cards 3, 6, 10 and the coordinate table on card 2 are also too small. Desktop is acceptable for all but the assembly sheet, where dimensions are still small.
issues.suggested_fix: Typed text for the words; show the drawing alone at full card width and open it zoomable (pinch/pan) by default for dense sheets.

issues.title: No image of the official drawn solution
issues.detail: After reveal the scheme is only a list of step names with marks ('Locate points Ph and Qh in plan and draw triangle 4m', 'Establish widths in plan 4m', 'Draw the cam profile 4m'). The SEC scheme for DCG is a worked drawing; none is shown on any of the 12 cards, so a student cannot see what the correct traces, strike/dip, end view or cam profile look like and cannot honestly tick the steps.
issues.suggested_fix: Show a crop of the official solution drawing for this part at the top of the scheme panel (zoomable), with the marked steps beneath it.

issues.title: Sibling parts visible on almost every card
issues.detail: Because the whole question is the image, other parts are shown in full: card 2 (asks d) shows a, b, c; card 3 (asks d) shows a, b, c; card 4 (asks a) shows b; card 6 (asks b) shows a, c, d; cards 7 and 9 show the other two parts; card 10 (asks a) shows b, c; card 12 (asks b) shows a; card 1 (asks b) shows all of (a) and card 8 (asks a) shows all of (b); cards 5 and 11 show (b). No different questions appear, only parts of the same question.
issues.suggested_fix: Type only the stem plus the asked part; keep the shared drawing.

good.why: Compact crop where text and drawing are both readable on desktop; five marked steps add to 17.
Short question, correct contour map attachment showing only the map, six ordered steps adding to 17.

more_issues: Sub-slice cards do not say what they cover
Raw scheme shorthand and terse labels
Dead space and wasted room on phone

issues.title: 'Scheme prints no answer' cards
issues.detail: Card 3 (5 marks, 2026 Q6) and card 4 (40-mark essay) show 'The scheme prints no answer for this part.' with a grey sentence ('The scheme reprints this question and prints nothing under it') and bare number buttons (0-5, or 41 buttons 0-40). The heading still says 'Select the points you actually got' and 'Select all — I had them all' though there are no points.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the general criteria for opinion answers/essays (content, coherence, language, accuracy with weightings), change the heading to 'Mark yourself', and use bands rather than 41 buttons.

issues.title: Grey language-rule note inside the scheme
issues.detail: 'The examination requires every answer in DUTCH. The paper prints the rule on page 3: "Alle antwoorden moeten in het Nederlands gegeven worden."' appears inside the first tick box of every card (above the content on cards 1 and 5, below it on card 2), and truncated in the attachment footer.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove from cards.

issues.title: Quotation and task run together
issues.detail: Cards 3 and 5 put the paragraph reference, a 3-4 line quotation and the actual question in one paragraph; on card 3 the quotation has no quotation marks at all, so it is hard to see where the quote ends and 'Ben je het daarmee eens of niet? Verdedig je standpunt.' begins.
issues.suggested_fix: Set the quotation as an indented block quote and the task on its own line.

issues.title: No marks on scheme points; leftover punctuation
issues.detail: Cards 1 (30 marks) and 5 (5 marks) list three points with no marks or criteria, so the tick boxes do not lead to a score. Card 1 keeps scheme typos: '–hedendaagse- media' and 'televisie.... etc.'.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the marking basis for the part; tidy the dashes and dot run.

good.why: Reference question with the paragraph cue, a one-line answer and the right text attached.
Three short, distinct scheme points that plainly answer the question.

more_issues: Essay rubric mentions several topics, shows one

issues.title: Attached page opens on a different question
issues.detail: The 'Official question page' attaches the whole printed page uncropped. The reader opens at the top of the page, which shows other questions in full before the card's own: card 2 (Q8(c)(i)) shows all of Q7 and Q8(a); card 3 (Q10) shows Q9 parts (i) and (ii) with Q10 only starting at the bottom edge; card 5 (Q6(ii)) shows all of Q5; card 6 (Q9) shows Q8 and its circular-flow diagram, Q9 not visible; card 7 (Q7(b)(ii)) shows all of Q6 and Q7(a); card 11 (Q6) shows Q4 and Q5, Q6 not visible. A student tapping the attachment sees the wrong question first and has to scroll to find theirs.
issues.suggested_fix: Crop the attachment to the card's own question region (or at minimum scroll/anchor the reader to it and grey out the rest). For plain text questions with no figure or table (cards 2, 3, 5, 7, 10) drop the attachment altogether: it adds nothing the text does not already say.

issues.title: Fill-in-the-blank question flattened, blanks lost
issues.detail: Card 6 runs the word bank and the gapped sentence together with no blanks: 'Utility Price Quantity Scarce resources Opportunity Cost Economic goods require the use of to produce them and so their use has an . Such goods command a in the marketplace.' It reads as broken English and the five terms are not distinguishable from the sentence.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the five terms as a row of chips or a bulleted list, then the sentence on its own line with visible blanks (____). Or show the official crop as cards 11/12 do.

issues.title: Attached page shows sibling parts and multi-page spreads
issues.detail: Where the page is the right question, it still shows every other part. Card 1 (Q14(c)(i), elasticity) opens page 1 of 3 on the Q14 inflation graph and part (a)(i), nothing to do with elasticity; the PED part is two pages on. Card 12 opens page 1 of 4 on Q14(a)(i)-(ii). Cards 4, 8, 9, 10 show parts (a)/(b)/(c) of the same question around the target.
issues.suggested_fix: Attach only the page (and region) that holds this part; for a multi-page question open on the page the part is on, not page 1.

issues.title: Bullets and sub-parts run into one paragraph
issues.detail: Card 4 prints the two scenario bullets inline ('...due to the following: • an unexpected heavy rainfall...; • breakdown of the main supply truck...') and then (i), (ii), (iii) as one long sentence in the large serif question style. The orange underline covers only an arbitrary middle slice of it. Card 5 keeps the paper's form text 'Yes / No. Place a circle around your choice' and then appends 'Justify the choice: YES.' which reads oddly.
issues.suggested_fix: Render bullets as a real list and (i)/(ii)/(iii) each on its own line. For the split yes/no card, rewrite the ask plainly: 'Assume you answered YES. Outline two reasons.'

good.why: Short clear question, clean chart crop limited to the graph, one-line scheme point with marks.
Three definitions, each a labelled tick with 5 marks; scheme answers the question exactly and fits one phone screen.

more_issues: Scheme heading and explanation glued together, raw slashes
Question shown only as a small picture on the phone; answer picture sits in the question area
Question refers to formatting or position that is not there
Mark rule stated two or three times, filler captions

issues.title: Internal authoring notes shown to the student in the scheme
issues.detail: Grey notes written for whoever built the cards are printed inside the marking points: card 4 'The paper sets two (c)s either side of an OR, the lathe chuck and the CNC lathe; the scheme prices their romans alike, (i) "Award 1 @ 5 Marks", (ii) "Award 2 @ 3+2 Marks"... so this card holds this part of both branches: claim the rows for the branch you answered.' Similar notes on cards 5 and 12, and on card 9 'The scheme answers this part with a drawing or notation its text cannot carry; its own print is shown with the answer.' In card 4 the note hangs under the first answer ('4-jaw independent chuck,') as if it explained it.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove these notes from student view. If guidance is needed, one plain line above the routes: 'This question offered a choice. Mark only the option you answered.'

issues.title: Stress-strain graph cropped without axis values or curve labels
issues.detail: 2022 HL Q3(b)(iii) asks to calculate Young's modulus for metal A and metal B. The figure shows only two coloured curves on bare axes: no stress/strain numbers, no units, no A/B labels. The scheme answers 260 and 60 kN/mm2, which cannot be derived from what is shown.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-crop the figure from the paper to include axis titles, scale values and the A/B labels, plus the stem line that introduces the graph.

issues.title: Heading glued to its sentence in scheme options
issues.detail: Option rows run a label straight into the body with no punctuation or break: 'Compression moulding A measured amount of thermosetting polymer...', 'Vacuum forming Vacuum forming is used...', '(i) CAD The term CAD...', '(iii) G Codes Determine the tool path', 'Crystalline solid structures Crystalline atoms are arranged in a pattern Amorphous solid structures Amorphous atoms are arranged randomly', and five rows in a row all starting 'Advantages of photovoltaic (PV) panels ...'. On the phone these become tall grey paragraphs.
issues.suggested_fix: Render the label as a bold title on its own line (or a group heading once: 'Advantages - any one, 4 marks') and the explanation beneath it.

issues.title: Either/or questions run together with a bare 'OR'
issues.detail: Two alternative questions are set as one paragraph: '...holding work on a centre lathe. OR A CNC lathe used for CAD/CAM technology is shown. Describe two advantages...'. It reads as one confusing question, and both pictures (chuck and CNC lathe; vehicle and beacon) sit side by side unlabelled. The scheme side handles it well with Route A / OR / Route B.
issues.suggested_fix: Mirror the scheme layout in the question: 'Option A' block, an OR divider, 'Option B' block, each with its own picture.

good.why: One-line question, six short tickable functions; clean on phone.
Typed question, official up-cut/down-cut diagram and two clear explanatory rows.

more_issues: Scheme diagram shown in the question column; tick row has no answer
Truncated and incomplete scheme rows
Leftover wording that depends on missing context

issues.title: Scheme has no question-specific content
issues.detail: Every card's reveal is the same generic material: 2-5 boilerplate tick-boxes ('Address every instruction in the printed task', 'Sustain a clear, purposeful response in an appropriate register'), a PCLM mark grid, and a grey box stating 'The published scheme prescribes no set content for this response'. For questions like 'Is this a disturbing poem?' or 'Do you agree family is important in Circle of Friends?' the SEC scheme normally prints indicative points; none are shown. The reveal therefore does not answer the question at all - it only lets the student guess their own mark.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the scheme's indicative material for this exact question (the 'Expect candidates to...' / 'Possible points' bullets), as clean bullets or as a crop of the official scheme entry, ABOVE the PCLM grid. If the scheme truly prints nothing, say so in one line and do not label it 'Possible directions'.

issues.title: Bulleted sub-tasks flattened into a dash-joined paragraph
issues.detail: Card 10 runs three required bullet tasks into the sentence: 'consider fascinating: - Describe how ... in the novel - Explain what ... the relationship - Suggest one piece of beneficial advice ...'. Card 12 does the same with the option list: 'The Spinning Heart: - I found the novel entertaining - I found the novel disturbing - I found the novel boring. Explain your response...'. The student cannot see at a glance that there are three separate tasks/options.
issues.suggested_fix: Render each dash item as its own bullet line, with the closing instruction ('Your response should demonstrate...') as a separate paragraph.

issues.title: Older grade grid has overlapping bands and no zero
issues.detail: For the 10-mark 2014/2015 cards the grid reads A 8-9-10, B 7-8, C 5-6, D 4-5, E 2-3, F/NG 1. 8 appears in both A and B, 5 in both C and D, and there is no 0 option, so a student cannot tell which grade a mark of 8 or 5 is. The 2011 20-mark grid and the post-2017 O1-O8 grids do not have this problem.
issues.suggested_fix: Use non-overlapping mark bands (and include 0), or show the official grade table as printed.

issues.title: Confusing boilerplate inside the scheme
issues.detail: Card 2's checklist and grid say 'Make the choice the paper prints (Selected direction: 1 of 2). Every choice is marked on the same grid.' - internal wording that means nothing to a student. 'Read and use the official source material supplied with the card' is similar filler. Multi-criterion grids also behave inconsistently: on cards 6 and 10 Coherence and Language are greyed out with 'Set Purpose first - it caps this criterion', on cards 2, 8 and 12 they are not.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop internal phrases; write the checklist from the question's own verbs (e.g. 'Chose Ifemelu or Obinze', 'Named three objects', 'Explained what each reveals'). Apply the cap rule consistently.

issues.title: Whole-letter cloze printed as one run-on paragraph

issues.title: Written-production scheme is a text block plus empty pickers
issues.detail: The mark ladder is printed as a run of grey lines ('5 marks: Communicative intention fulfilled. / Good level of vocabulary. issues.suggested_fix: Show the ladder once as a small table (marks / what it looks like), and label each picker with the actual turn or point from the question. Drop the cross-references to other questions.

issues.title: Multi-part schemes are one flat list with no part headings or marks
issues.detail: On cards that combine (i), (ii), (iii), the scheme is a single run of tick rows with no indication of which part each belongs to or what it is worth. Card 11 has 13 rows: 'Advantages:' and 'Disadvantages:' appear only as a prefix on the first row of each group, and the health risks and the fixes for part (ii) follow with no heading at all. Card 10 mixes the orbital sander description, sander safety, pillar drill safety and the Repak answer in four unlabelled rows (the pillar drill has safety features but no description row). Card 2's three rows map to (i), (ii), (iii) but are not labelled, and 20 marks are not split.
issues.suggested_fix: Group the rows under '(i) - x marks' / '(ii) - y marks' headings, with 'Any one of these' sub-groups for advantages, disadvantages, risks and reductions, as the Engineering cards do with 'One of these - 4 marks'.

issues.title: Several required answers squeezed into one comma-joined row
issues.detail: Card 3 asks for three elements of a URL and offers one 8-mark row: 'https:// - Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure, www. - worldwide web, rugbyworldcup.com - domain/host name, /supporters - filename'. Card 5 asks for two reasons and offers one 6-mark row joining two reasons and 'etc.'. Card 4 has 'Assembly operations- materials handling, clamping work, packaging operations, etc.' as one row. The student cannot tick what they actually got, and the dashes and commas read as a strung-together line.
issues.suggested_fix: One row per element or reason ('https:// - Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure'), under 'Any three - 8 marks'; a two-column term/meaning layout suits the URL card.

issues.title: Drawing answers: tick row repeats the question plus an internal note
issues.detail: Where the scheme is a circuit or flowchart, the only tick row is the question text again ('Show how the given circuit could be modified...', 'Complete a flowchart for this sequence.') with the grey note 'The scheme answers this part with a drawing its text cannot carry; its own print is shown with the answer.' The actual answer drawing is in the left column under the question, and on the phone it comes before 'Your answer' and the scheme heading, so the 10-mark flowchart has no breakdown at all.
issues.suggested_fix: Put the scheme drawing inside the scheme panel under 'Model answer', replace the note with tickable features (relay added; mains supply and fan motor on relay contacts / each decision and process box in order), and drop the internal wording.

issues.title: Bullet list flattened into the stem paragraph
issues.detail: Card 9's alarm sequence is printed as running text with inline bullets: 'sequence: • when the engine stops, wait 2 minutes, ... ; • if the driver is not present ... ; • if a child is present ...'. Card 10 does the same in the question: 'material processing tools: • Orbital sander • Pillar drilling machine.' The sequence is the core data for the flowchart and is hard to follow on a phone.
issues.suggested_fix: Render the bullets as a real list, one step per line.

issues.title: Long grey editorial note before the first point
issues.detail: The first scheme box opens with up to 13 lines of small grey text on the phone: the answer-in-Ukrainian rule quoted in full, 'The scheme heads its answer "Наприклад:": what it gives is an example, not a required list', and then the scheme's lead-in sentence quoted inside the note. issues.title: Very long phone scroll and no marks per point
issues.detail: Scheme points are full paragraphs of 6 to 12 lines each on a phone, so cards 1, 4 and 5 run to about two and a half phone screens after the reveal. No point carries a mark, so the student ticks points and is then told to 'assess your complete answer against the 5-mark total' without guidance on how many points are enough.
issues.suggested_fix: Give each point a short bold summary (three to six words) with the full text beneath, and say how many points a full-mark answer needs if the scheme says so.
